input: A defect-reduction project carried out on a filling line succeeded in cutting the reject rate from 3.1% to 1.6% over the course of one quarter. When the improvement is applied to the line's throughput of 195k units per year, it is found that the reduction avoids approximately 2925 rejected units per year. Each avoided reject represents a filled unit that passes inspection in the normal way rather than being diverted to rework or scrap, and it is important that the reject rate has been measured on an identical inspection basis both before and after the change, so that the comparison is a valid one. The annual saving figure is obtained by applying the reduction in rate to the annual volume, and it should be understood as the saving that will accrue provided that the lower reject rate is maintained in normal operation. One qualification must, however, be recorded: the quarter in question included a planned shutdown, and no adjustment has been made to the rates on that account. The rates therefore relate to a quarter in which the line was in production for fewer days than a complete quarter, and it remains to be seen whether the improvement will be sustained when uninterrupted running is resumed; the figures for the following quarter, measured on the same basis, will provide the answer.
target: A defect-reduction project on a filling line cut the reject rate from 3.1% to 1.6% over one quarter. At the line's volume of 195k units per year, the reduction avoids about 2925 rejected units per year. An avoided reject is a filled unit that passes inspection instead of going to rework or scrap, and the rate is measured on the same inspection basis before and after the change, so the comparison is between like quantities. The annual figure is the product of the rate reduction and the annual volume: it is a rate of saving at the lower reject level, and it holds only while the lower rate is maintained in normal running. The quarter included a planned shutdown, and the rates are not adjusted for it. The measured rates therefore come from a quarter in which the line ran fewer production days than a full quarter, and the reduction is stated as measured over that quarter, not as a full-quarter equivalent. Whether the lower rate survives the return to uninterrupted running is not settled by the quarter's figures; the next quarter, measured on the same basis and without the shutdown, is the check on it. The reduction is claimed as measured, with the shutdown stated alongside it wherever the figure is reported.
